paper_metadata.title: Hybrid Quantum–Classical Support Vector Machines for Financial Regime Detection: Performance and Efficiency Evaluation

summary: The paper evaluates a 6‑qubit ZZFeatureMap QSVC for financial regime classification on macro‑financial data (2006–2025). The quantum SVM achieves about 66% test accuracy versus ~65–72% for classical ML baselines and ~80% for a classical SVM, while hybrid quantum‑classical ensembles reach ~75–76% accuracy but remain below the classical benchmark. All experiments are performed on noiseless Qiskit statevector simulation.

experiments.description: Quantum Support Vector Classifier (QSVC) for financial regime classification using a 6-qubit ZZFeatureMap and fidelity-based quantum kernel on macro-financial data.

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Six standardized PCA components were mapped to six qubits; the ZZFeatureMap encodes pairwise feature interactions via phase terms x_i x_j with full entanglement.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Binary market-regime classification maximizing SVM margin in the quantum-induced feature space using kernel K(x_i,x_j)=|<phi(x_i)|phi(x_j)>|^2.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: SMOTE oversampling used to balance classes; no explicit penalty formulation reported.

problem_instance.description: Binary financial regime detection (Bearish -1 vs Bullish +1) from multi-asset macro-financial indicators.
problem_instance.dataset_name: SPY, VIX, 10Y Treasury yield, 2Y Treasury yield, high-yield credit spread, DXY

dataset_specification.preprocessing: returns, rolling volatility, z-scores, momentum, moving-average ratios, volatility-of-volatility, skewness, kurtosis; winsorization at 1st/99th percentiles; z-score standardization; PCA to 6 components; SMOTE 0.6; chronological 80/20 split

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: StandardScaler, PCA to 6 orthogonal components, SMOTE oversampling ratio 0.6, chronological 80/20 split, winsorization at 1st/99th percentiles, z-score standardization before kernel computation.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Single held-out chronological test set; accuracy, precision, recall, F1; confusion matrices; training vs test comparison; scalability comparison across sample sizes (2,000 and 3,500).

implementation_details.classical_solver: classical SVM optimization on kernel matrix
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Inverse mapping of encoded labels; confusion matrices; metric computation
implementation_details.total_execution_time: kernel matrix evaluation ≈3 minutes; full QSVC training reported ≈1 hour (Methodology 3.3.5) and ≈120 minutes in Results 4.4.5

speedup_claims.factor: poly(log N, log d) vs polynomial scaling
speedup_claims.conditions: assuming efficient QRAM, sparse and well-conditioned matrices, and accurate amplitude encoding
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper does not demonstrate an asymptotic speedup; it explicitly notes that the assumptions are highly restrictive and that practical quantum advantage is not yet realized.

speedup_claims.factor: approximately 3 minutes vs about 1 hour to 120 minutes for full quantum training
speedup_claims.baseline_method: full quantum kernel training on CPU-based statevector simulator
speedup_claims.conditions: for the reported 6-qubit, 3-repetition QSVC on approximately 3,500 samples
speedup_claims.caveats: This is a runtime comparison, not a quantum speedup over classical methods; it reflects optimized simulation and kernel evaluation timing.

complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: not explicitly stated; classical SVM baseline reported as much faster and scalable on CPU
complexity_analysis.wall_clock_quantum: approximately 3 minutes for kernel evaluation; full training reported as about 1 hour to 120 minutes depending on section
complexity_analysis.wall_clock_classical: approximately 1 second to under 1 minute for classical baselines

advantage_assessment.crossover_size: not identified; classical baselines outperform at current dataset size (~3k samples)
advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Would require larger qubit counts, deeper circuits beyond 6 qubits and 3 feature‑map repetitions, and real QPU implementations with efficient kernel evaluation.
limiting_factors: No demonstrated algorithmic speedup (kernel evaluation O(n^2))
Statevector simulator rather than real hardware
Quantum model accuracy (~66%) below classical baselines (~65–72% and SVM ~80%)
Potential overfitting due to limited sample size and circuit expressivity

notes: hardware.type inferred as simulator_statevector because the paper explicitly says the QSVC was run on a noiseless statevector simulator and no physical QPU is named.
speedup_order set to none_proven because the paper discusses practical limitations and does not claim a demonstrated asymptotic quantum speedup.
circuit_depth taken from the feature-map repetitions (3 repetitions) since no separate circuit depth metric is reported.
Paper reports QSVC test accuracy ≈66%, while classical models reach up to ≈71.8% (XGBoost) and ≈80% for classical SVM baseline in later comparisons.
Authors explicitly frame quantum models as exploratory and not outperforming classical methods.

experiments.description: Hybrid quantum-classical SVM ensemble combining a classical RBF SVM with the QSVC via hard voting and weighted voting (50-50, 60-40, 70-30).

algorithm.variant: Hybrid Quantum-Classical SVM ensemble with hard voting and weighted voting

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Quantum branch uses six PCA components encoded on six qubits with ZZFeatureMap; classical branch uses RBF kernel on the same standardized PCA features.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Binary regime classification with ensemble aggregation of classical and quantum predictions.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: SMOTE balancing; deterministic hard/weighted voting; no explicit penalty terms reported.

problem_instance.description: Binary financial regime detection on the same macro-financial dataset as the QSVC experiment, evaluated with hybrid ensemble aggregation.
problem_instance.dataset_name: SPY, VIX, 10Y Treasury yield, 2Y Treasury yield, high-yield credit spread, DXY

dataset_specification.preprocessing: same engineered features as the quantum experiment; StandardScaler, PCA to 6 components, SMOTE 0.6, chronological 80/20 split

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Same preprocessing as the quantum experiment: engineered returns/volatility/momentum features, winsorization, z-score standardization, PCA to 6 components, SMOTE 0.6, chronological split.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Held-out test set; accuracy, precision, recall, F1; confusion matrices; agreement analysis between classical and quantum predictions; runtime comparison; evaluation of 50-50, 60-40, and 70-30 ensembles.

implementation_details.classical_solver: classical SVM-RBF plus quantum kernel classifier combined by voting
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Hard voting and deterministic weighted voting; agreement statistics; confusion matrices; metric aggregation
implementation_details.total_execution_time: classical SVM about 1 second; hybrid runtime a few seconds to minutes depending on weighting; quantum component trained on subset only
implementation_details.quantum_execution_time: subset-based quantum kernel evaluation; exact time not separately reported

speedup_claims.factor: near-classical accuracy at lower quantum participation
speedup_claims.conditions: for hybrid 50-50 and 60-40 ensembles on the held-out test set
speedup_claims.caveats: The hybrid models do not exceed the classical SVM in accuracy; the paper frames the result as a trade-off between accuracy, fairness, and computational cost.

speedup_claims.factor: few seconds to minutes vs about 120 minutes for full quantum training
speedup_claims.conditions: hybrid training with the quantum component restricted to approximately 2,000 samples
speedup_claims.caveats: Runtime is reported qualitatively for the hybrid ensemble; exact per-configuration times are not given.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: quantum component inherits O(n^2) kernel evaluation
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: classical SVM training reported as approximately 1 second on CPU
complexity_analysis.wall_clock_quantum: few seconds to minutes for hybrid; full quantum component much slower than classical baseline

advantage_assessment.crossover_size: not identified; hybrid accuracy (~75–76%) still below classical SVM (~80.4%)
advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Potential advantage would require scalable quantum kernels, larger qubit systems, and faster kernel evaluation beyond classical simulation.
limiting_factors: Hybrid accuracy (~75–76%) lower than classical SVM (~80%)
Quantum component trained on small subset (~2000 samples)
Statevector simulation rather than hardware execution
Limited circuit depth and qubit count

notes: hardware.type inferred as simulator_statevector because the quantum component is the same QSVC statevector-simulator setup described in the methodology/results and no physical device is named.
circuit_depth taken from the 3 repetitions of the ZZFeatureMap; no separate compiled depth is reported.
speedup_order set to none_proven because the paper emphasizes a cost-performance tradeoff rather than a proven asymptotic advantage.
Hybrid models improve minority‑class F1 compared with pure QSVC but still underperform classical SVM in overall accuracy.
Authors describe hybrid models as a 'bridge to scalable quantum applications' rather than evidence of advantage.
